summary: Checked the item's first step (Vieta-type automorphisms of the ES surface). The ES surface F = 4xyz - n(xy+yz+zx) = x(4yz - n(y+z)) - n*yz is linear in each variable, so each (y,z)-fibre has at most one x and no Markoff-type second root exists; the repo already records this (toric model with one point per side, 'no involutions', only S3 visible). Also contrasts MARKOFF_ES.md's S_{n,D}, which has fibrewise Pell orbits only.

summary: Not actionable: 1/R = 1/x+1/y+1/z with R = n/4 is literally the ES equation, a restatement with no new test. Checked the natural Belyi candidates: the Fermat curve of exponent p is a (p,p,p) cover with chi = 3/p - 1 (not 4/p - 1); X(p)/X_0(p) have cusps (2,3,inf)-type. Every ES triple has x,y,z > p/4, so for p > 4*M0 (M0 = largest entry in Takeuchi's finite list of arithmetic triangle groups, Tak77 Thm 3; exact M0 not checked) no ES triangle group is arithmetic, and no finite-index subgroup can be a congruence/Shimura-curve uniformisation: the modular-Belyi route is closed for large p. Dessins with ES passport are not thereby excluded (Assessment).

The repo has both (B2_ACROSS_FIELDS.md line 87 says log^2, z31_unit_fractions.md §(c) says log^3); the expected-count comparison itself is already recorded there. summary: Read Machiavelo-Tsopanidis arXiv:2003.02592 (abstract, Thm 1, Thm 2, Prop 5-7). Their mechanism is Legendre's three-square theorem applied to N(zeta)m - n^4 in the Lipschitz order, plus congruence handling of the linear square condition mod 3 and 5. The ES quaternion form has reduced discriminant p*e (QUATERNION_ES.md l.24-34), so no ternary reduction with exact local-global counts is available; the step did not transfer.

Gauss's three-triangular-number theorem is already tabulated against ES in the repo: universal existence via 8n+3 and three squares, but the representation count is class/L-value scale and not uniformly power-sized, unlike the needed reservoir. Theta-quotient comparison not repeated.

ES has no group action (Vieta moves absent, Z0082 lemma: F linear in each variable), so there is no fundamental-set reduction to transfer. The 'does ES escape the mechanism' question is answered at memo level there.

summary: Not actionable: EKL measure rigidity gives dimension/a.e. statements for real-parameter multiplicative approximation; ES is a single-n integer existence question. The second step 1/y+1/z = (4x-n)/(nx) is a divisor problem, with no diagonal action in sight.

Checked the Heegner-type first step (a curve E_p mapping to the ES surface). The ES affine part V_n is isomorphic to G_m^2 (GEOMETRY_ES.md §2.2), and any regular morphism from a complete curve to G_m^2 is constant (coordinates would be units on a projective curve). So a naive E_p -> ES map is excluded; a rational map defined off a finite set of points is not excluded by this argument (Assessment).

Primitive divisors of Lucas sequences are already analysed in the repo: a primitive divisor l at index t satisfies l = (D/l) mod t (z45 §1.2), so divisors of u_{4C} lie in classes +-1 mod 4C, with the sign fixed by a Jacobi symbol. This is a sign condition, not a construction of divisors of 4Cp+1, and BHV is catalogued at z45 §B.

Zsigmondy/Bang divisors and their forced cyclotomic classes are covered in the same z45 memo (§B). The polynomial prime-divisor construction for -1 mod 4C reduces to the Lucas sign condition already recorded for Z0430.

MENU_LADDER.md (l.26) already excludes a Grunwald-Wang exception for exponent 2: a nonzero element that is a local square at almost all places is a global square (Chebotarev), so the 2-adic residue obstructions relevant to square classes do not produce a Grunwald-Wang-type failure. T1 phrasing remains open as the repo says.

Calibration only: for fixed p, ES(p) is a bounded finite search and so decidable; the uniform statement over p needs variable products (ab = 4Cp+1 with a, b, C, p all varying), outside the Presburger/Buchi fragments. No concrete test was identified.

QUATERNION_ES.md already identifies the Type I order Lambda_{d,m} with reduced discriminant pe, index e in maximal orders, and records that the discriminant grows with p (the 'bad' case); Gross-Zagier factorisation is excluded by coprimality (l.38). The Eichler-mass positive main term is therefore on an order whose discriminant depends on p.

technique_transfer_list.md item 9 already records that Hooley-type sums sum_c tau(p^2+4c^2 d) are not known uniformly in the constant term, and that the condition f = -p mod 4cd is a moving-modulus event (collapses to H-A/B2).

Polynomial identity families for 4/n are covered by the (J)3/(J)78/(J)79 menu-closure theorems and their Gaussian follow-up (z35): identities with irreducible top-degree part cannot reach infinitely many primes. The proposed degree-<=3 Groebner computation would re-derive a closed case, so it was not run.

METAPLECTIC_ES.md §4-5 already analyses the Thm K generating function: the summed series sum_{t,u,v>=2} q^{tuv-u-v} is a shifted d_3-type GL(3) Eisenstein object with no holomorphic or half-integral component carrying the main term, and the exact signed expansion R = E + O - B (E>0) is the H-E lane. Nonvanishing is therefore already reduced to the H-A/B2 object.

Read LMU arXiv:2311.10008 (v4). Their families are diagonal affine cubics a1 u1^3 + a2 u2^3 + a3 u3^3 = a0 with BM obstructions via Hilbert symbols, not ES-type surfaces (the ES surface has no diagonal form and no triangle-of-lines model matching theirs). Their failure counts therefore do not calibrate ES.

BRAINSTORM/addcomb_unit_fraction_density.md §3.1 already shows Bloom's Prop 1 needs N^{1-o(1)} terms, against 3 for ES, and the memo verdict is COLLAPSES to B3. Liu-Sawhney's dense-set results (item Z0224) also have unbounded term counts.

Box search over Z[i] (script z52b_p1_L00_gauss_es.py) for 4/pi = 1/xi + 1/eta + 1/zeta over Gaussian primes of norm <= 200. Without the cone condition 87/89 primes have identities at R=8 (median hits 20 at R=8, 54 at R=30), but the same box over Z gives 16/46 at R=8: an artefact, since Bradford-Ionascu note ES is trivial without a cone. With the Bradford-Ionascu cone (Re*Im>0 for each denominator), the hit fractions are 0.34 (R=8), 0.38 (R=16), 0.38 (R=30) over Z[i] and 0.11, 0.22, 0.37 over Z (positive ES), i.e. no Gaussian advantage at R=30. 86% of no-cone hits satisfy pi | zeta, which reduces to the two-term problem and occurs equally over Z (86%). Nothing new beyond the repo's assessment.
